milestone: Explicit rank-one CPU tensor construction from runtime numeric arrays
implementation: ArrayToTensor typed IR requires completed homogeneous numeric CPU array input and preserves element type and rank-one extent facts while changing the source category. CPU MLIR uses checked byte counts and an ordered extract/insert copy into a fresh logical tensor. Contextual fixed extents use existing ShapeCheck/precondition machinery before allocation. Continuation kernels and imported synchronous map/helper graphs remap the input operand. No checked ABI, scheduler, ownership runtime or numeric engine changes.

contract.syntax: tensor(values) or values -> tensor(); values may come from numeric map and feed tensor arithmetic/reduceSum.
contract.types: Six numeric CPU element types. No implicit array/tensor coercion or element conversion. Runtime construction is rank one; existing scalar and ranked literal constructors retain their behavior.
contract.length: Same element count, source order, raw representations and private extent facts. Typed empty arrays construct empty tensors. Fixed expected extents reject known mismatches and check unknown lengths before result allocation.
contract.ownership: Current lowering makes a checked copy; borrowed native input storage does not escape as an owned result. Input remains unchanged. Owned output may outlive source invocation and worker.
contract.failures: No partial output on shape, allocation or cancellation failures. Arithmetic in callback helpers preserves its source. Checked worker failures recover through existing TaskError handling.
contract.workers: Direct spawn tensor(values), constructor in ordinary worker helpers and imported anonymous callback graphs, nested workers, cached awaits and retained result tensors. Ordinary argument expressions evaluate before dispatch.
contract.scope: CPU rank-one numeric arrays only. Runtime reshaping, tensor-to-array conversion, arbitrary nested-array data and GPU/mixed-target array construction remain gated.

qualification.scope: Focused array/tensor, map/closures, numeric frontend, source/task/recovery, control-flow, storage and selected Metal regressions; not the full suite.
coverage: Six numeric input/result identities checked and lowered with preserved dynamic lengths and explicit array-to-tensor category changes.
Typed empty arrays, fixed/dynamic extents, contextual scalar and ranked literal regressions, pipeline syntax and constructors inside nested anonymous callbacks.

Shared rank-one borrowed-input oracle from ArrayMapRuntimeTests.cpp checks exact boundary/random raw bits (including signed zero, subnormals, infinities and NaN payloads), eight ARM FP environments, strided input immutability, allocation-failure sweeps and retained output.
Fixed extent harness tests original-source Shape faults before allocation and exact copies independent of subsequent borrowed-input mutation, with retained owners and allocation failure.
Negative extents, overflowing byte counts and exact byte-bound allocation failure; cancellation before entry and during an active million-element copy, with no partial result or mutated input.
Six numeric worker families exercise map/constructor/reduction helpers, constructor inside imported/nested closures, direct and nested workers, cached awaits and exact retained tensor layouts.
Empty mapped arrays skip a faulting callback. Original-source Arithmetic faults and runtime Shape faults recover through supervised workers.
1/2/4-worker success, cancellation, deadline and admission checks; core allocation positions 1-8 plus generated invocation allocation positions 1-8 with two workers.
Invalid runtime reshape, element mismatch and implicit reduction inputs preserve existing output artifacts. Malformed IR input IDs, category, shape and element metadata are rejected.
Debug, optimized, ASan/UBSan and separate ThreadSanitizer execution, sanitized frontend and prior map/array/tensor/numeric/frontend/worker/selected Metal regressions.

remaining_gates: Runtime tensor reshaping and explicit runtime shapes
Tensor-to-array construction and broader collection element types
First-class function values and broader native types/modules
Native distributed execution requires design discussion
